summary: @c1-ease/core ships a postinstall and import-time beacon to a hardcoded VPS endpoint
details: The package consists of a no-op Proxy export (index.js) and a beacon module (beacon.cjs) that fires both from the declared postinstall lifecycle script and on require of the main module. The beacon collects installer host identifiers — hostname, install path, current working directory, and node/npm version — and POSTs them as JSON to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc, with TLS certificate verification disabled (rejectUnauthorized:false). The destination is a bare Contabo VPS unrelated to any documented service, and the package provides no functional API: every property access on the exported Proxy returns a no-op function, so the only observable effect of installing or importing @c1-ease/core is transmission of installer identifiers to that endpoint. The scoped name mimicking a generic compatibility 'core' shim is consistent with dependency-confusion or typo-bait targeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
